claims.content: Customer

The auction listing interface is documented as requiring the actor to be authenticated with the Auctioneer role and logged into the Auction Administration workspace; the available evidence does not document a distinct Customer-role entry path or authentication precondition for this listing workflow.
The system has a populated inventory of items with images and defined categories (e.g., Jewelry, Gemstones, Watches).
All active auction items are searchable by all item attributes, including product ID, auction number, product category, product type, stone type, metal type, current price, and full-text description.

After the successful listing operation, the system sets the item's auction status to 'Scheduled' when the assigned start date/time is in the future, or to 'Current (Live)' when the auction is immediately active.

After the successful listing operation, the system populates the item's auction metadata with Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve price, High Bid (initially $0.00 if no bids yet), # of Bids (initially 0), and Winner / High Bidder (blank until a bid is placed).

The listed item appears in the auction administration interface's searchable results table of active or scheduled auctions, with columns including Action (checkbox), Image, Product ID, Auction #, Description, Open Bid, High Bid, Unit Cost, Starts, Ends, Duration, Product Type, and Increment; scheduled (not yet live) rows are highlighted in blue.
The listed jewelry item is displayed in the 'Today's Top Jewelry Auctions' module on the homepage with a visible price and an active 'Bid Now!' button.

claims.content: The Customer initiates the use case by clicking the 'My Current Bids' link in the top navigation bar, which leads to the 'Auction Administration' workspace, where the Customer performs a product search using filters (e.g., Retail Category: Jewelry) to find eligible items, selects one or more returned items via the checkboxes in the 'Action' column, and chooses an action from the scrolling 'Action' list box (e.g., 'Create grouping / event') to initiate the listing.

The primary objective of the use case is to allow a Customer to list personal jewelry items for auction by selecting them from a searchable inventory and initiating an auction action (e.g., 'Create grouping / event') via the Auction Administration interface.
